cards.title: World Notes: Knights and Courtesy
cards.sub: A real thing behind one of our books
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read with your lens in mind.
text: The word courtesy comes from the word court, the place where a king or queen lived. Long ago, people at court were expected to have good manners.
Old stories about knights say a good knight was brave and polite: he bowed, kept his promises, and helped people in need.
Despereaux learned to say “I honor you” from a book of stories like these. That is courtesy, knight style.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it's Opti. Today you make your writing stronger, and you get to give out some awards.
transcripts.guide1: Word work: build words, fix a sentence out loud, and find spelling mistakes.
transcripts.guide2: Revise your opening and one paragraph. Write your closing. Then give out the Bookshelf Awards.
transcripts.guide3: Write your notes for sharing out loud.

notes.wordParts: Word parts I know: -y and -ness mean being something, -ous means full of, -ful means full of, -less means without, un- means not, re- means again.
notes.grammar: Editing checklist: capitals on names and the first word, apostrophes for belonging and joined words, a comma before and/but/so when it joins two complete thoughts, and the right past form, like went.
notes.spelling: Find the base word first. Then check what was added: drop the silent e (hope, hoping), double the last letter (hop, hopping), change y to i (cry, cried), or add -es (box, boxes).
notes.wgrd: A strong closing says your claim in a new way and tells what the character teaches us about good character.
vocab: doing the right thing even when no one is watching
understanding and sharing the feelings of another person
the ability to keep going after something hard
